clue.text: Alternative PM that represents England for Shakespeare?

definitions.meaning: read literally, the phrase describes a different ..., Anthony ... having been a British Prime Minister
John of Gaunt's description of England in Richard II

explanation.surface: A rival prime minister who stands for England in a Shakespeare play.
explanation.walkthrough: Anthony Eden was a 1950s Prime Minister, so a second one would be another Eden; in Richard II, John of Gaunt calls England 'this other Eden, demi-paradise'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is John of Gaunt's famous description of his country in Richard II, likening it to paradise.

clue.text: Joint almost broken with doubled force

indicators.note: almost the whole word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: something broken is split

indicators.note: doubled means the letter for force is written twice

parts.note: F is the physics abbreviation for force

explanation.surface: A joint in the body nearly broken by twice the force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' looks like a body part, but it is the slang word for a cannabis cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: A joint is slang for a cannabis cigarette, which is also called a spliff.

clue.text: A stirring race meeting?

parts.note: a pot that is stirred where races meet and blend: a society mixing many peoples

explanation.surface: An exciting day at the horse races.
explanation.walkthrough: 'race meeting' suggests horse racing, but the races here are peoples, and 'stirring' is the cook's spoon in the pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A melting pot is a society where different peoples and cultures mix together into one.

clue.text: Bird's periodical food

parts.note: a periodical is a magazine, a mag for short
a pie is a type of food

explanation.surface: A bird's regular meal.
explanation.definitionFit: The magpie is a black-and-white bird of the crow family.

clue.text: Apostle meeting God? It's child's play

parts.note: Peter was one of the twelve apostles
Pan is the Greek god of the wild

explanation.surface: An apostle meets God, and it turns out to be easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'child's play' looks like the idiom for something easy, but means a play for children.
explanation.definitionFit: J. M. Barrie's Peter Pan is a stage play written for children.

clue.text: Youth spotted this problem

parts.note: spotted means covered in spots, the skin condition common in teenagers

explanation.surface: A young person noticed a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spotted' reads as noticed, but means marked with spots.
explanation.definitionFit: This skin condition, causing pimples, typically afflicts teenagers.

clue.text: I prove criminal American gets a police record

indicators.note: criminal suggests something bent or wrong, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: US is short for American, as in the United States

explanation.surface: An American prisoner protests innocence while having a criminal record.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, having previous means having earlier convictions, a record held by the police.

clue.text: Dolls are scattered round outhouse: one should be in cabinet

indicators.note: round means the jumbled letters go around the other piece
scattered letters are spread out and rearranged

parts.note: a privy is an outdoor toilet, an outhouse

explanation.surface: Dolls left lying around an outbuilding, one of which belongs in a display cabinet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scattered' rearranges the letters of DOLLS ARE; 'cabinet' is the government's Cabinet, not a display case.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lord Privy Seal is a senior British minister who traditionally sits in the Cabinet.

clue.text: Break one's word

parts.note: split a word into parts with a dash, rather than fail to keep a promise

explanation.surface: Fail to keep a promise.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom means renege, but taken literally it is splitting a word at a line end.
explanation.definitionFit: To hyphenate is to join or divide words with a hyphen, as at the end of a printed line.

clue.text: Dog number ten, a rare item

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
ten written as the figures 1 and 0 looks like the letters I and O

explanation.surface: A dog with the number ten tag, an unusual object.
explanation.walkthrough: The figures 10 are read as the letters IO.
explanation.definitionFit: A curio is an unusual or rare object valued as a curiosity.

clue.text: Change loose dress

explanation.surface: Change into a loose dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Shift means alter position, and is also a simple loosely hanging dress.

clue.text: Kept quiet, being shy

parts.note: P stands for piano, the musical direction for quiet
a shy person is reserved

explanation.surface: Kept silent because of shyness.
explanation.definitionFit: Preserved food is kept from spoiling, so kept and preserved are synonyms.

clue.text: The indignant take it as a violation

definitions.meaning: a breach of a law or rule

explanation.surface: Angry people treat it as a breach.
explanation.definitionFit: To take offence is to feel insulted; an offence is also a crime or infringement.

clue.text: See 1
Get snappy here when very warm in rear of ship

indicators.note: in means one piece sits within the other

parts.note: the poop is the raised deck at the stern of a ship
very warm is hot

explanation.surface: Getting irritable when it's sweltering at the back of a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snappy' suggests bad temper but means taking snaps, photographs.
explanation.definitionFit: A photo op is an occasion staged for taking photographs, a place for snapping pictures.

clue.text: No square dealings in this seat of power?

definitions.text: No square dealings in this seat of power?

parts.words: No square dealings in this seat of power?
parts.note: a room with no corners, being oval rather than square, where the US president works

explanation.surface: A suggestion of dishonest goings-on at the centre of government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No square dealings' suggests crookedness, but means the room is not square.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oval Office is the US president's oval-shaped workroom in the White House.

clue.text: See 8
Agitated by the disorder at university

indicators.note: disorder means the letters are put out of order

parts.note: to be up is to be in residence at university

explanation.surface: Upset by unrest on campus.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone het up is excited and agitated, an informal idiom.

clue.text: Bill sounds cheap for pictures

parts.note: a tab is a bill, as at a bar

indicators.note: sounds means the word is said aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: low prices are cheap

explanation.surface: A bill seems to be low-priced for the paintings.
explanation.definitionFit: Tableaux are scenes or striking groupings, like living pictures.

clue.text: Part of a Dutch name for a vehicle

definitions.meaning: ... is the particle in Dutch surnames such as ... Gogh

explanation.surface: A Dutch name element used for a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Van means 'of' in Dutch surnames, and is also a covered road vehicle for goods.

clue.text: Another royal pulled down, one in Africa

parts.note: Victoria was a British queen
something pulled down falls

explanation.surface: Yet another royal is toppled, this one in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Victoria Falls is a huge waterfall on the Zambezi between Zambia and Zimbabwe.

clue.text: When spoken endlessly, very Italian

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he left'

indicators.note: endlessly means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: something spoken is said

explanation.surface: When said without stopping, something is very Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: Assai is the Italian musical term meaning very, as in allegro assai.

clue.text: Such repetitive work attracts no living wage

definitions.text: Such repetitive work attracts no living wage

parts.words: Such repetitive work attracts no living wage
parts.note: machines doing mechanical tasks are paid nothing at all

explanation.surface: A complaint that monotonous jobs pay too little to live on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no living wage' sounds like poor pay, but machines doing the work earn no wage at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Robotic work is mechanical and repetitive, the kind done by machines.

clue.text: Naughtily fool guy with mystery science

indicators.note: naughtily suggests misbehaving letters that get out of place

explanation.surface: Mischievously tricking a man with occult knowledge.
explanation.definitionFit: Ufology is the study of unidentified flying objects, a pseudo-science of mysteries.

clue.text: Scruffy representation of nudity

indicators.note: a representation reshapes the word, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A scruffy depiction of a nude.
explanation.definitionFit: Untidy and scruffy are synonyms for messy in appearance.

clue.text: Shout at youngster climbing platform in the sea

parts.note: oi is a shout to get attention

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the word reads upward, backwards

parts.note: a girl is a youngster

explanation.surface: Yelling at a child clambering on a sea platform.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'climbing' signals reading upward; 'oi' is a British shout for attention.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil rig is an offshore structure for drilling, a platform out at sea.

clue.text: Military command contemplates where armies clash

parts.note: to eye something is to look at it, contemplate it
the front is where opposing armies meet in battle

explanation.surface: An order that considers the battle lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyes front is a parade-ground order to look straight ahead.

clue.text: See 1
Took a tumble from deadly hill

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective means cruel or deadly
a hill or moor in northern England

explanation.surface: Fell off a deadly hill.
explanation.definitionFit: Three senses: fell as fallen, fell as savage (one fell swoop), fell as upland.

clue.text: See 19 down
See 8
The quality is not entirely the same

indicators.note: not entirely means only part of these words is used, letters lying within them

explanation.surface: A quality that is only partly the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are equal are identical in value, the same.

clue.text: Had coin in change for part of south-east Asia

indicators.note: change means the letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone had coins in their change for a region of Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Indochina is the peninsula comprising Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia and neighbours.
